hypothesis: A single elected representation may learn useful disagreements between several model families by retaining true labels and also learning their out-of-sample probabilities. Compare to the same representation with genuine labels and to an equally mixed uninformative probability. Research candidate only.
design: Reuse the seven audited upstream methods fitted exclusively on 2685 training rows. The existing group-disjoint roles are unchanged. On the 1319 nomination rows choose a cloneable logistic student by its classification accuracy; choose the best single teacher or unweighted pair of teachers by Brier loss, preferring fewer teachers on ties. Use actual candidate probabilities without names or model-specific policies. The 1319 nomination labels are excluded from all student fits. Apply the frozen teachers to the 1318 other, previously unseen teaching rows. Check probabilities against their independently recorded ordered digests.
fits: Fit three copies of the same elected student to the same 2685 original and 1318 new labelled rows. Keep original labels for all original rows. On the 1318 teaching rows compare (1) original labels, (2) half label plus half uniform, (3) half label plus half frozen teacher probability. Mirror pair orientations consistently. Preserve the same total supervised sample weight across arms. Reuse only label-free pretrained embeddings; recompute the feature pipeline from the 4003 student rows without using any evaluation row. At most three new local classifier fits and no model API.
decision: After all three fitted models are frozen, evaluate the 1309 disjoint former audit groups' rows. Require the teacher-trained student to beat both controls on accuracy before purchasing the independently sealed 1670 other training rows. Only after sealing all outer predictions may the latter labels be read. On both panels report corrections and regressions separately versus both controls. Require a win versus both on both panels and at least +0.20 percentage points pooled versus true labels before another trial. Panels belong to a previously studied development corpus and do not constitute a new course-designated grade. No course validation, formal test or H2.
